And that part I know firsthand, which very few people applying this year can say.

The three weakest words in any argument are people say, and I hear them every week. The reason they are weak is not that they are vague, although they are. It is that there is nobody there to disagree with. If you tell me that people say the first month is the hardest, I can simply reply that other people say the opposite, and we are both finished, because neither of us has said anything that can be checked. Now watch what happens when you attach a person. My coach, who has sent four players abroad, told me the first month would be the hardest. That is a sentence I have to answer. And notice which half is doing the work: it is not the name, because I do not know your coach. It is the role. Who has sent four players abroad is the part that explains why this person would know anything, and without it the name is decoration. One warning, and it is the one I care most about. When you carry somebody else's words, you do not get to improve them on the way. An argument you win by making somebody's quote slightly better than it was is an argument you lose completely the first time anybody checks.

Three people told me something before I left, and I remember all three because I have thought about them a lot since. My coach told me the football would be the easy part, and he was right, and he was also the only one of the three who had actually done any of this. A friend told me I would be fluent in three months. He said it twice, because I did not believe him the first time, and he had never left the country in his life. And an adviser at school told me to sort the paperwork out early, which sounded boring and was the most useful sentence of the three. Obviously the one I believed was the friend, because it was the one I wanted to hear, and that is the honest answer to why. So the thing I do now is very small. Before I take advice from anybody, I ask them how they know. Four seconds. And it separates the people who have done the thing from the people who have opinions about the thing, and it turns out those are almost never the same group.
